target_customer: Large enterprises, especially banks and manufacturers in Japan, where non-engineer staff build internal AI workflows
problem: Enterprise teams want to automate workflows with AI but drag and drop builders need engineers and lack enterprise controls.
business_model: B2B SaaS with credit based workflow execution tiers, an enterprise plan and on-prem or private cloud deployment

founders.name: Shoya Matsumori
education: Ph.D. in computer science per YC profile (launch post says machine learning)
founders.background_notes: Named as representative director of Carnot in the 2023 funding coverage.

competitors.name: Dify
competitors.what: Open source LLM app and workflow builder with an enterprise edition resold in Japan
competitors.traction_then: Kakaku.com reported about 950 internal apps built by employees (vendor case study)

competitors.name: n8n
competitors.what: General workflow automation with AI steps

technical_complexity.rationale: Natural language to workflow generation, integrations, permissions, audit logging and on-prem deployment are standard but broad engineering; the enterprise security work is the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Enterprise deployments with SSO, audit logs and bank customers create integration and compliance lock in, but the core workflow builder concept is widely copied.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Workflow builders were already adding AI agents in 2025 and 2026; no outcome yet for Jinba.

market_need_then: Japanese enterprises were adopting generative AI internally in 2025; the company reports 40,000 enterprise users at major financial institutions and logos such as MUFG Bank, Toridoll and Suntory on its site (self reported).

branding.domain_note: Product site jinba.io; legal entity is Carnot AI, Inc. with the Japanese entity Carnot.

identity.logo: not described by any source found
identity.visual_style: enterprise SaaS site, bilingual English and Japanese
identity.voice_and_tone: plain enterprise tone with a playful footer line, Built in San Fransokyo

branding.brand_signature: San Fransokyo footer line tying the San Francisco and Tokyo teams

brand_strength.rationale: Product name differs from the company name Carnot, which splits identity; no press about the brand itself found and the name origin is unknown. Jinba Ittai, a Mazda phrase, shows up in search and may confuse, but no source links it to the company.

outcome_analysis: Jinba is an active Winter 2026 company that grew from the Japanese startup Carnot, which raised a pre-seed in July 2023 and later joined YC. It reports large enterprise usage in Japanese finance, which suggests an early enterprise sales motion. No exit or failure has occurred; the open question is whether it can stay ahead of Dify, n8n and platform vendors.
notes: The 2023 pre-seed was reported as 85 million yen; amount_usd left null because no USD figure is stated by the source. Preqin lists an undisclosed seed in 2026-03 from Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund, and CB Insights lists a 0.5M convertible note dated 2025-12-17 but could not be tied to this entity; both are aggregators and not recorded as rounds. Jinba was founded as Carnot in Oct 2022 per the Initial database. Competitors were dated 2026 only from vendor and blog pages, so as_of is approximate.
